title: Reproducing LiTS Crosswords
subtitle: Local failure analysis and terminal-state preservation
body: FTEC5660 / 22 October 2026
notes:
Hello, I am WU Yile. This project reproduces the execution of the LiTS crossword chain with a free local model. The initial prompt experiment produced a negative result. An audit then uncovered a specific state-reporting defect, which I isolated and repaired. I will distinguish the live model experiment from the offline software replay. Both are backed by saved evidence, and the repair does not mean that the language model became a successful crossword solver.

Sources: results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: Reproduction target
body: LiTS Crosswords chain, Table 3
Reported word accuracy 10.33% and puzzle exact match 6.67%
Original setup uses Claude 3.5 Sonnet on 30 puzzles
This study substitutes a free local model and ten fixed puzzles
notes:
The assignment permits a meaningful subset and a substituted model when the change is documented. I chose the authors' runnable chain implementation and compared its metrics with the published reference. Because the model, quantization and subset differ, I do not treat a score difference as a verdict on the paper. The local experiment did not recover the paper's numerical performance. It does reproduce executable action selection, environment transitions and validation behavior. Source: Li and Tao, 2026, Table 3, https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-demo.5/.

Sources: https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-demo.5/; results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: A terminal error hides the observed board
body: The model makes a valid placement and the board changes
Repeated invalid proposals create a terminal error step
That error step has no next_state snapshot
The original accessor returns the initial empty board
notes:
The important defect lies between the agent loop and the state accessor. The agent stores each executed action together with its resulting board. If validation later fails three times, the loop appends an error step with no new board. The current-state accessor inspects only the final step, so it falls back to the initial board. Earlier snapshots still exist in the history. This makes an error look as if no placement had ever happened. I traced this behavior in the pinned source and reproduced it with a separate deterministic test. Sources: EnvChain.run and EnvState.env_state in the pinned LiTS repository.

Sources: results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: Live experiment and paired offline replay
body: Live study: ten puzzles, three seeds, two prompts
60 actual model episodes and 227 inference calls
Follow-up: replay all 30 original-prompt episodes
Original and fixed accessors read identical recorded steps
notes:
The first study was fixed before the measured outcomes. It compares the original prompt with one added letter-consistency instruction, using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct in four-bit MLX format. Seeds are seventeen, forty-two and two thousand twenty-six. The step limit is ten and temperature is zero point eight. After the failures exposed the accessor issue, I wrote a separate follow-up protocol. That follow-up replays all thirty original-prompt episodes. It generates no new model responses. I explicitly disclose that the repair hypothesis arose during debugging rather than claiming it was preregistered with the original study. Sources: PROTOCOL.md, PROTOCOL_STATE_FIX.md and both experiment configurations.

Sources: results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: One isolated accessor change
body: Original: use the final step snapshot, otherwise the initial board
Fix: use the most recent recorded snapshot, otherwise the initial board
The terminal error and all model calls remain visible
No prompt, transition or word proposal changes in replay
notes:
The patch replaces the final-step lookup with a reverse search through the recorded steps. It returns the first nonempty snapshot. When there was no successful placement, it still returns the initial board. I keep the error step and do not reclassify an unsuccessful episode as a solved puzzle. The replay asserts identical initial states, actions and observations in each pair. This isolates one software change. The submission includes both an equivalent subclass for replay and a small patch that applies to the upstream source. Source: scripts/replay_state_fix.py and patches/preserve_terminal_snapshot.patch.

Sources: results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: The fix recovers recorded partial progress
notes:
The plot shows character accuracy by seed before and after the accessor repair. The original final boards are all empty. The preserving accessor recovers 1.73% mean character accuracy, with a sample standard deviation of 0.83 percentage points. Eight episodes had an observed placement, and all eight recover their last observed board. The other twenty-two had no placement to preserve. This is a reporting correction. Word accuracy remains zero, and I do not present the recovered letters as improved language-model reasoning. Source: results/state_fix/summary.json.

Sources: results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: Preservation improves, task success stays zero
notes:
The table separates a successful software repair from unsuccessful model behavior. The original accessor retains none of the eight nonempty terminal boards, while the fix retains all eight. Complete-word accuracy remains zero and all thirty original-prompt episodes retain their terminal validation-error flag. The same 116 existing model calls support both views. The replay uses zero additional calls. The full live study uses 227 calls across sixty episodes, at zero paid API cost. Local inference timing includes rejected attempts but excludes downloading, model loading and warm-up. Sources: the live and state-fix summaries.

Sources: results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: Recorded trajectory: puzzle 6, seed 17
notes:
This trajectory executes four valid placements before an invalid proposal exhausts the retries. The original accessor shows an empty board. The preserving accessor returns the last observed board, which contains two correct letters out of twenty-five, or 8.00% character accuracy. None of its complete words is correct. This case has the largest character-score difference and illustrates the mechanism rather than the typical task performance. Every cell comes from the saved trajectory or the benchmark answer key. Source: results/main/baseline_s17_p006.json and results/state_fix/summary.json.

Sources: results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: The original prompt intervention did not help
body: Final word accuracy: 0% under both prompts
Invalid proposal rates: 89.35% and 89.75%
All 60 live episodes ended in a validation error
All final scores agree with an independent evaluator
notes:
I preserve the failed initial experiment because hiding it would give a misleading account of the project. The extra instruction required consistency with visible letters, but the local model frequently violated the five-letter or action-format requirement before that instruction could help. Many calls repeated the same invalid answer. The zero word scores also remain zero after recovering the observed state, so the accessor defect does not explain away the model's poor complete-word performance. An independent evaluator agrees with the official final-grid scores. The small sample and three seeds support a descriptive result, not a broad significance claim. Sources: results/main/summary.json and raw call logs.

Sources: results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.

title: Conclusions and limits
body: The original multi-step workflow runs with a free local model
A small accessor fix preserves all eight affected boards
Word accuracy and validation failures remain unchanged
Model and subset changes limit comparison with the paper
notes:
The assignment asks what reproduces, what does not and why. The runnable environment and error behavior reproduce. The paper's reported numerical accuracy does not reproduce under this substituted local setup. The isolated fix improves the fidelity of the final state while preserving failure status. A deterministic software test using known answers confirms that the environment and official checker can reach a solved state, but I exclude that answer-key test from model performance. Future work should test a stronger model or constrained output separately. The repository includes pinned assets, protocols, complete calls, trajectories, independent scoring and the patch. AI assistance supported this package, and the student should review it and personally explain the result. Thank you.

Sources: https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-demo.5/; results/main/config.json; results/main/summary.json.
